summary: Restored branch_ledger and configured node1 as the sole writer with node2 as a read-only MariaDB replica. Replication, disconnect catch-up, exact row preservation, write denial, credential scoping, export preservation, and sequential restart persistence were directly verified.
actions_performed: Installed RHEL-compatible MariaDB 10.11.18 without changing the OS release or kernel.
Restored the original ledger rows 1001=12.50 and 1002=-3.25.
Configured ROW binary logging on node1 and persistent read-only replication on node2.
Created a node2-scoped replication-only account and restricted node1 TCP/3306 access to node2.
Verified disconnected catch-up with no missing or duplicate IDs.
Verified live inserts before and after both node restarts.
Safely restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and confirmed changed boot identities and full recovery.
Removed temporary credentials, transport keys, probe accounts, and test files.

evidence.requirement: Restore the staged ledger and preserve the export
evidence.summary: Original IDs and amounts remain intact; ledger.sql remains 196 bytes with SHA-256 fcd54ac91dff5010c8dda0ddfa5cf2586d2d172456c7ca8ca33d0bffabc73700 on both nodes.

evidence.requirement: Use compatible software without replacing the OS or kernel
evidence.summary: MariaDB 10.11.18 from RHEL repositories runs on RHEL 10.0 with the retained 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 kernel.
repl_ledger is restricted to node2 and has REPLICATION SLAVE only; data and administrative privileges are absent.

evidence.requirement: Node2 is read-only and node1 is the sole application writer
evidence.summary: Application-style inserts succeed on node1; node2 rejects them with MariaDB error 1290 and creates no forbidden row.

Committed rows arrived automatically before and after restarts. Final source and replica contain 6 unique IDs, sum 98.10, and matching canonical SHA-256 eb3f7ff068ad1173ece3e367b421a9a354e292c486aaa50476b849969c207887.

evidence.requirement: Catch up after a short disconnect without loss or duplication
evidence.summary: The replica I/O thread was stopped, two rows were committed on node1, and node2 caught up to the exact source position with 4 rows and 4 distinct IDs.
Boot ID changed from 7217fc31-8b1e-4097-936b-13f98cd8a5df to 4a00b5ba-af96-4cea-9414-6c1f2209418a; MariaDB, data, export, listener, binary logging, and replica connectivity recovered.
Boot ID changed from 2b19e976-dee2-4700-9045-90d61b6dcffe to bd223214-17e9-4caa-a114-2e882db765e0; MariaDB returned read-only with exact data, healthy IO/SQL threads, and zero lag.
